correctness.rationale: For two-level unitary evolution p_01(t)=p_10(t)=a sin²(omega t/2). Under exponential inter-probe times, nonnegative kernels K=re^(−rt)p(t), L=re^(−rt)(1−p(t)) yield exact renewal equations f_tr=K+L*f_tr and f_ret=L+K*f_tr. Their survival difference equals G_r*(delta_0+sum_{n>=1}L^{*n}), G_r(t)=r e^(−rt)[(1−a)t+(a/omega)sin(omega t)]. The positive renewal measure implies stochastic order for every rate iff the seed is nonnegative for all times, and its first negative sinc minimum occurs uniquely at z* in (pi,3pi/2) with tan z*=z*, giving a*=1/(1−sin z*/z*)=0.821534976... . Necessity uses fixed-t small-r expansion at t=z*/omega, plus initial positive rt term to force crossing. A separate exact Laplace transform comparison proves return < transition in Laplace order for all a,r, including the crossing regime; means differentiate from the same transforms. Independent symbolic renewal-transform identity and local root/sign calculations supported the analytic proof. Finite tests are not a substitute for the all-r,t arguments.

value.rationale: This gives a sharp quantitative boundary at which return detection ceases to dominate transition detection at every finite time, despite retaining strict Laplace transform order. The separation is a natural and nontrivial probabilistic phenomenon for experimentally motivated randomly probed quantum dynamics; it supplies a threshold and unavoidable crossing mechanism not answered by existing mean or long-time tail optimizations.

scientific_limitations: Only coupled two-level Hermitian Hamiltonians, ideal projective Poisson probing, pure initial preparation and detection targets |0> vs |1>.
Above-threshold crossing is proved for sufficiently small interrogation rates, not all rates.
